title: Ilocos Pink Peanut (NSIC Pn 12): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Ilocos Pink Peanut: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Ilocos Pink peanut is a peanut variety. About 96 days to harvest, 1.6 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Ilocos Pink is a registered peanut variety, also sold or known as NSIC Pn 12. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2003 as NSIC 2003 Pn 12. It takes about 96 days from sowing to harvest, with 1.59 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Ilocos Pink peanut takes about 96 days from sowing to harvest. That is 5.8 days faster than the average of the 26 peanut varieties with a day count, 101.3 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 1.59 t/ha trails the average of its group, 1.85. It sits in the lower quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives about 95 to 96 days.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It was weak against cercospora leaf spot, so scout for it from the early weeks.

The pests and diseases that hit peanut fields most often: [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [eggplant leafhopper](/pests/eggplant-leafhopper), [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
A hundred seeds weigh about 57 grams, so the higher this number, the bigger the seed. The seed holds 32.58 percent crude protein.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** 1.72 t/ha dry season, 1.47 t/ha wet season.
**Fruit:** About 47 to 57 g per 100 seeds, about 71 to 73 percent shelling, crude protein about 32.6 percent.
Resistant to rust, moderately susceptible to Cercospora leaf spot.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: Ilocos Norte's registered peanut, with the highest protein in the registry list. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Ilocos Pink peanut

It is recommended for both the wet and the dry season. Mani needs loose, well drained soil to fill its pods. Pick a variety by seed size for your buyer, and one rated against rust and leaf spot for the wet season.

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is NSIC Pn 12 the same as Ilocos Pink?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Pn 12 is another name for Ilocos Pink, registered as NSIC 2003 Pn 12. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 96 days from sowing to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 1.59 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Ilocos Pink?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
